ideas.name: KneeWall Pivot Bracket (self-levelling shelf/hook bracket for sloped attic walls)
ideas.concept: A pair of stamped/laser-cut powder-coated steel brackets with a toothed pivot that locks the shelf level on any wall pitch from about 30 to 75 degrees, plus a built-in bubble gauge and a fixing plate that lands on a rafter or a batten. Sold as a bracket pair, or as a bracket pair plus oak shelf.
ideas.target_customer: Loft converters and owners of rooms with sloped walls and roof windows in SE/DK (snedtak/skraavaeg), plus loft-conversion installers who fit out kids' rooms and kitchens.
ideas.problem_solved: Standard shelf brackets assume a vertical wall. On a sloped wall the shelf tilts or the owner pays a carpenter. Danish handyman price data shows DKK 500-1,250 to hang two floating shelves in a sloped-wall kitchen (single quote-site figure, Low confidence).
ideas.moat_mechanism: Utility model/design on the locking pivot geometry. German Gebrauchsmuster costs EUR 30 online and lasts up to 10 years (DPMA, seen via search), and an EU registered design costs EUR 350 (single-design fee, several law-firm sources). I estimate EUR 500-1,000 for a prior-art search (ASSUMPTION). HONEST LIMIT: a 6-month copycat can design around a tooth-and-pivot claim, and the registered design only stops look-alikes. The claim will only stand if the pivot is genuinely novel, which has to be checked before filing. Defensibility 3 at best.
ideas.trend_evidence: Danish Bolius advises on making the most of sloped walls and notes that special brackets exist (seen only as a search snippet; the page could not be fetched). A Swedish IKEA reviewer notes that wall angles differ and fixed-angle brackets do not fit. Loft conversions are an ongoing Nordic renovation theme. No search-volume data could be obtained (Firecrawl and Ahrefs unavailable), which I could not verify. I found no dedicated pivot bracket on SE/DK retail sites in the searches, but did not exhaustively check Amazon.
ideas.price_point_eur: 35-39 per bracket pair (ASSUMPTION); 59-69 with oak shelf
ideas.channel_edge: Loft-conversion contractors and roof-window installers from the ex-VELUX network recommend and resell it. Build-your-own-attic content on Instagram/TikTok. Shopify plus a DK/SE builders' merchant pilot. A B2B pair at about EUR 20 leaves low CAC.
ideas.est_landed_cost_eur: 7-10 per pair (ASSUMPTION, Low confidence; quote needed from an EU/PL or CN metal job shop)
ideas.est_first_order_eur: 3,500-4,500 for about 400 pairs plus oak shelf samples, with a separate EUR 1,000-1,500 for IP search and filing
ideas.one_off_tooling_eur: 800-1,500 (laser-cut plus press-brake fixtures and pivot tooth die; ASSUMPTION; a progressive die would exceed budget and is avoided)

ideas.name: WoodSafe Clamp Carrier (non-marking blind/pleated-shade carrier for tilt-turn and roof-window sashes)
ideas.concept: A clamp bracket with a wide, articulated pressure pad that spreads clamping force, adapts to rounded or lipped sash profiles, and carries a 5+ mm stand-off so the blind clears the handle. Replaces the rectangular-profile clamps used by no-drill pleated-blind sets.
ideas.target_customer: Renters and owners with wooden tilt-turn windows (DK/SE/DE housing), and online blind sellers who need a clamp their own blinds do not damage frames with.
ideas.problem_solved: Search results show standard clamp carriers can permanently damage wooden frames, only fit rectangular profiles and rubber-gasket windows (fold depth 16-25 mm), and the handle needs a 5 mm clearance. The alternative, glue-on carriers, needs 24 h to cure.
ideas.moat_mechanism: EU registered design (EUR 350) plus a possible utility model on the articulating pad geometry. HONEST: weak. Competitors such as Klemmfix-style systems are established and a pad redesign is easy to copy. The real edge would be a bulk supply or licence agreement with a blind maker, not IP. Defensibility 2.
ideas.trend_evidence: selbst.de explains the clamp-versus-glue choice and the frame-damage caveat for wooden windows; a forum post (bau.de) flags that round frame edges are hard for standard clamps; a Klemmfix instruction PDF states fold depth 16-25 mm and the 5 mm handle distance. No sales or search-volume data was available.
ideas.price_point_eur: 22-29 for a 4-clamp retail set (below the EUR 35 preference); B2B 8-11 per set (ASSUMPTION)
ideas.channel_edge: Mainly B2B: sell or license to blind makers and DIY chains that already stock pleated blinds, using the founders' negotiation skills. Retail alone cannot carry CAC at this price.
ideas.one_off_tooling_eur: 3,000-4,500 (small injection mould for the pad and a stamped spring clamp; ASSUMPTION; near the edge of the allowed range)

ideas.name: Koppelhake Retrofit Clip (repair clip for Swedish coupled-window hooks), B2B for housing associations
ideas.concept: A snap-on or screw-on repair part that restores a broken or worn hook/eye between the inner and outer sash of coupled windows (kopplade fonster) without removing the sash. It is sold in bulk packs with a gauge card to caretakers and property managers.
ideas.target_customer: Swedish bostadsratter (BRF) boards, property managers (fastighetsskotare) and renovators of older wooden windows.
ideas.problem_solved: Hook repair is a recurring BRF maintenance topic. One BRF guide describes a temporary Velcro fix, a permanent swap to the right hook type, and a warning that a new hook type can widen the gap between the sashes.
ideas.moat_mechanism: The channel, not the IP: bulk supply plus a sizing gauge to housing associations the founders can reach through VELUX-era building-industry contacts. A design registration (EUR 350) on the retrofit clip adds little. A hardware wholesaler could stock a copy. Defensibility 2, only if a framework deal with a property-management company is signed.
ideas.trend_evidence: A BRF (bostadsrattsforening) repair guide and a brf maintenance check PDF on the topic were seen. Retail hooks exist at Bauhaus, Bygghemma, Ahlsell (24.5 mm diameter noted in the search summary), but the price page could not be fetched, so I could not verify prices. Retail hook prices are probably low (ASSUMPTION), so only a bundle with the gauge card and fitting tool is viable.
ideas.price_point_eur: 35-49 for a 10-hook caretaker box with gauge and tool (ASSUMPTION); no consumer price below EUR 15
ideas.channel_edge: Direct outreach to BRF boards and property managers; one framework deal is worth more than retail. Founder building-industry relationships are the real edge.

ideas.name: Roof-Window Rain-Hush Kit (damping pads plus tested installation spec for roof-window rain drumming)
ideas.concept: A kit of die-cut viscoelastic/butyl damping pads and a mounting template for the metal cladding and sash edges of roof windows, with a published dB-reduction test report.
ideas.target_customer: Attic-bedroom owners with roof windows, and installers who get complaints after a roof-window installation.
ideas.problem_solved: Rain and hail noise on roof windows is a recurring forum complaint; common fixes are an external awning blind or special noise-reducing glazing, both costly.
ideas.moat_mechanism: An independent acoustic test report (EUR 2,000-3,000 at an accredited lab, ASSUMPTION; competitors would have to pay the same to make the claim) and a damping material spec. HONEST: damping sheet material is a commodity and the claim is unproven. Effectiveness is unvalidated, so run a cheap pre-test first and kill the idea if under 3 dB. Defensibility 2, Low confidence, and a risk of OEM objection if it touches the glazing warranty.
ideas.trend_evidence: Several UK forum threads (Google Groups uk.d-i-y, Mumsnet, DIYnot-type forums, MoneySavingExpert) discuss rain noise on roof windows; one says an awning blind helps; a triple-glazed unit was quiet but still audible in rain. These are UK sources, old, and not Nordic. No sales data.
ideas.channel_edge: Roof-window installers and the dealer network (ex-VELUX) as an upsell after install; owner forums. B2B CAC low if installers adopt it.
ideas.est_first_order_eur: 2,000-3,000 for about 300 kits plus EUR 2,000-3,000 lab test

ideas.name: Wind-Rated Wall-Sleeve Flap (passive back-draught flap for kitchen exhaust wall boxes)
ideas.concept: A stainless spring-and-magnet flap insert for 125/150 mm kitchen-hood wall sleeves that closes tight in wind and opens at low fan pressure without rattling.
ideas.target_customer: Homeowners with cold draughts through extractor-hood exhaust, and installers/ventilation contractors.
ideas.problem_solved: German forum threads describe cold air through the exhaust duct and rattling flaps in wind; one source says passive flaps rattle and active flaps cost more.
ideas.moat_mechanism: A utility model on the spring-magnet closing mechanism (EUR 30 DE online, up to 10 years) and a wind/low-pressure test report that competitors must also pay for (ASSUMPTION, EUR 1,500-2,500). HONEST: backdraught flaps are an established commodity category; fire-safety certification may be needed; the source forums appear AI-generated (flagged by the search itself), so demand evidence is Low confidence. Defensibility 2.
ideas.trend_evidence: Seventeen bau.de/bau.net forum threads on 'Dunstabzug zieht' were returned, but the search engine flagged them as AI-assisted forum content, so demand is unverified. No Nordic sources checked.
ideas.channel_edge: Ventilation installers and building-industry contacts for B2B recommendation; weak on TikTok.
ideas.one_off_tooling_eur: 1,500-3,500 (stamped stainless parts and magnet fixture; plastic mould avoided)

ideas.name: Balcony-Door Gust Stop (three-position wind latch and child ajar limiter for balcony/terrace doors)
ideas.concept: A surface-mounted latch with three positions: closed-locked, 8 cm ajar for ventilation, and a wind-hold open position, which stops balcony doors slamming in gusts and lets them be vented safely.
ideas.target_customer: Apartment dwellers and housing associations with balcony/terrace doors, and parents wanting the door ajar but not open.
ideas.problem_solved: A bau.net thread on retrofitting a terrace-door stopper cites injury risk from gust slams and notes that a ventilation stopper is not a lock. Existing options include a Bauhaus balcony-door catch and the reer WinLock child lock (Rossmann).
ideas.moat_mechanism: EU registered design (EUR 350) plus a possible DE utility model (EUR 30) on the three-detent mechanism. HONEST: crowded with existing catches and baby-safety locks, a competitor can design around it, and no independent standard was verified. Defensibility 2.
ideas.trend_evidence: bau.net thread on terrace-door stoppers; sanier.de guide to balcony-door adjustment; products exist at bauhaus.at and rossmann.de. Nordic demand not verified.
ideas.channel_edge: Housing-association bulk packs; Amazon DE/SE; weak organic social.
